Build the calendar app in /home/max/ws/mine.

Mine is a set of PWAs storing personal data as markdown in a private GitHub repo. The
main app, the sync layer (shared/) and on-device platform verification are done and
proven end to end against the real repo. The calendar is a stub. Build it.

Read first — these are the spec, follow them rather than inventing:
  REQUIREMENTS.md, TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md           (root: architecture, findings)
  calendar/REQUIREMENTS.md, calendar/TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md
  shared/store.js, shared/github.js, shared/md.js      (the API you build on)
  calendar/sample/                                     (the exact file format)

Scope for this session:
 1. calendar/data.js — turn the local mirror into entries: parse, expand RRULE over a
    date range, apply overrides (series + recurrence-id), exdate/rdate, resolve groups
    via groups.md; and create/update/delete entries, including path generation (4 random
    chars, recurring/ vs the date tree).
 2. calendar/index.html + app.js — month view and the entry popup (create, edit, delete,
    tick a task done), group filter, top pane with the dropdown date picker.
 3. Responsive from the start — on a phone, coloured dots and a bottom sheet, not a
    shrunken desktop grid. Do not retrofit this afterwards.
 4. Vendor rrule into shared/vendor/ and record it in shared/vendor/VENDOR.md.

Leave for later: day/week/year views, calendar/widget.js.

Hard constraints:
 - No build step. Plain ES modules, relative imports, every page opens from disk.
 - CSP is script-src 'self': no inline <script>, no inline handlers, no CDNs ever.
 - Parse frontmatter only via shared/md.js. It loads YAML with CORE_SCHEMA because
   js-yaml's default turns `start: 2026-04-18` into a JS Date at UTC midnight, which
   shifts every all-day entry a day east of UTC.
 - rrule.js works in UTC. For an all-day rule read the UTC year/month/day; calling
   getDate() on a local Date returns the previous day east of UTC.
 - A filename is never the source of truth for a date — frontmatter `start` is. After a
   move or an override the two legitimately disagree.
 - All writes go through github.js write()/remove() then drain(). Never call the GitHub
   API directly; the queue, conflict handling and atomic commits live there.
 - Don't modify spike/ or the sync logic unless you find something actually broken.

Deploying and testing:
 - git push deploys to GitHub Pages in ~60s: https://maximilianharr.github.io/mine/calendar/
 - Bump VERSION in sw.js whenever cached files change, or devices keep serving the old
   copy, and add the calendar's new files to the SHELL precache list.
 - Data repo is maximilianharr/mine-data. It is a development repo, not anyone's real
   calendar, so seed it freely with whatever data makes the views worth looking at —
   several groups, all-day and timed entries, a weekly recurring task with one occurrence
   skipped and one ticked.
 - /home/max/ws/mine/.env.secrets holds GITHUB_OWNER/REPO/BRANCH/TOKEN for testing. It is
   gitignored — never commit it, never echo the token. Use it from node to seed entries
   and to verify that what your write path produces is exactly what your read path parses
   back, including a title with umlauts.
 - You have no browser. The month grid, the popup and the bottom sheet can only be tested
   by Max on an iPhone and a Pixel, so finish by telling him exactly what to tap.

Done when, on a phone: you can create an event and a task, see them in the month view in
their group colours, tick the task done, edit and delete them, filter by group, and a
weekly recurring task appears every week with a single occurrence skippable and tickable
independently of the series — all committed to mine-data as markdown matching the shape
of calendar/sample/.

########## REQUIREMENTS.md
# Mine

Mine is a set of PWAs (Progressive Web Apps) to digitalize ones personal or professional life.
The key idea is to save everything in a repo as markdown files. This can be calendar entries,
diaries, markdowns extracted from voice recordings / pdfs / .. These .md files can easily be
ported to new apps without a vendor lock-in and are processed via an (AI) assistant to help you
plan your day, keep track of tasks, remind you of memories a.k.a. a second brain.

To keep complexity to a minimum each use-case lives in a separate folder. e.g. the calendar PWA
lives completely in a 'calendar' folder as does the zettelkasten and all the other apps. Each
folder contains a 'sample' folder with samples how the markdowns shall look, a REQUIREMENTS.md
describing how the PWA works and a TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md describing how it is built.

See [TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md) for how this is built.

## One app, one setup

Mine installs as **one** app on the phone, with one icon. The apps in the subfolders are pages
inside it, not separate installs.

This is what makes the central requirement work: **the GitHub repo and token are entered once,
in the main app, and every app in a subfolder uses them.** Verified on iPhone and Android.

## Main app

A tile per app: its `icon.svg` above its folder name.

Above the tiles, apps may contribute a summary. The calendar's shows today's entries and the
next one — which matters, because opening the app is the only reminder that works (see below).

## First run

1. Open the app URL and add it to the home screen (iOS: Share → Add to Home Screen;
   Android: menu → Install).
2. The setup screen asks for GitHub owner, data repo, branch, and a personal access token.
3. The app tests the connection and reports clearly if it fails.

Settings are stored on the device only. The token is never displayed again after entry, and the
app warns 14 days before it expires.

## Using it

- Changes appear instantly and are queued for GitHub in the background.
- A sync indicator shows: in sync / pending / error.
- Offline, the queue is kept and sent when you are back online or reopen the app.
- Editing the same entry on two devices never loses either version: the other device's version
  keeps the file, yours is kept beside it, and the app asks which to keep.
- Everything works offline, including dates and search, because the app keeps a full local copy.

## Reminders

**Mine cannot notify you while it is closed.** No browser can schedule a notification for later;
this is a platform limitation, not a missing feature. Alerts are stored with each entry and
exported, and they fire while the app is open. The summary on the tile screen is the reminder.

## Updates

When a new version is deployed the app shows "Update ready — reload". It never updates while you
are in the middle of editing.

## Privacy

Your data lives in a **private** repo. The app itself is public, but it contains no data, and the
token is scoped so that it can only touch the data repo.

########## TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md
# Mine — technical requirements

How [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md) is built. Everything here was verified against the live
API or on device on 2026-11-19; `spike/` re-runs the device checks and needs no token.

## Repos

| Repo | Visibility | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maximilianharr/mine` | public | this app, served by Pages at `/mine/` |
| `maximilianharr/mine-data` | **private** | the markdown data |

Pages cannot serve a private repo without Enterprise, so data in the app repo would be
world-readable at a predictable URL. The token is scoped to the data repo only.

## Layout

One `manifest.json` with `scope: /mine/`, one service worker at the root. Subfolders are ordinary
pages inside that scope. `/mine/` and `/mine/calendar/` are the same origin, so they share one
IndexedDB — that is the whole mechanism behind "enter the token once".

```
/index.html /manifest.json /sw.js
/shared/  apps.js  store.js  github.js  md.js  vendor/
/calendar/  index.html  app.js  widget.js  icon.svg  sample/
```

No build step: no bundler, no CI, no node_modules. `git push` deploys, every page opens from
disk, all paths relative so the `/mine/` prefix needs no config.

`shared/apps.js` exports the app list and is imported by both the tile screen and `sw.js`, so
adding an app means editing one array. An app may export `summary()` from `widget.js`.

## Bootstrap — 1 request

One GraphQL query returns an app folder's tree **with contents and blob SHAs**, nested to the
depth of the layout:

```graphql
repository(owner:$o, name:$r) { object(expression:"main:calendar") {
  ... on Tree { entries { name type object {
    ... on Tree { entries { name type object {
      ... on Tree { entries { name type object {
        ... on Blob { oid text isTruncated } } } } } } } } } } }
```

- `rateLimit.cost` is **1** however many files return — `entries` is not a paginated connection.
  A 16 MB / 145 file response came back in 6 s without error.
- `Blob.oid` is byte-identical to the REST tree SHA, so this single request also supplies the
  SHAs that pulls diff against and writes send as their base.
- Check `isTruncated`: GraphQL truncates very large blobs and returns `text: null` for binary.
  Fall back to a REST blob fetch for that path.
- An **empty repo** returns `object: null` rather than an error, and `defaultBranchRef: null`.
  Treat it as an empty mirror, not a failure.

**Do not use the tarball.** `GET /tarball/{ref}` 302-redirects to `codeload.github.com`, which
answers `access-control-allow-origin: https://render.githubusercontent.com` — one specific
foreign origin. `fetch()` applies CORS to the final response after the redirect, so it is
blocked, and the preflight an authenticated request needs returns 403. `api.github.com/graphql`
by contrast sends `allow-origin: *` and a 204 preflight allowing `Authorization`.

**A repo with no commits rejects the Git Data API outright.** Not just the ref read — `POST
/git/blobs` itself answers 409 "Git Repository is empty", so there is nothing to build a tree
from. Only `PUT /contents/{path}` can create the first commit. The first queued file goes that
way, and everything after drains normally once a history exists.

## Pull

1. `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{branch}` with `If-None-Match`. A 304 means nothing changed and
   costs no rate-limit quota.
2. On 200: fetch the tree, diff blob SHAs, fetch only changed files, drop deleted paths.

Run on app open and on window focus. Background Sync does not exist in Safari, so all syncing is
foreground.

## Writes — one commit per drain

Queue each change locally with the blob SHA it was based on, then drain the whole queue as one
commit via the Git Data API: `POST /git/blobs` per file, `POST /git/trees` with `base_tree`
(deletion = entry with `sha: null`), `POST /git/commits`, `PATCH /git/refs/heads/{branch}` with
the expected old SHA and **no force**.

One drain is one commit, so a move — delete plus create, because the date is in the path and the
API has no rename — cannot be half-applied, and a 20-item offline backlog is one commit.

A rejected ref update means someone pushed elsewhere: pull, rebuild on the new base, retry. This
succeeds, because nearly every write is a create at a freshly generated path.

**True conflict** = a queued change whose base SHA no longer matches the remote blob. Remote keeps
the canonical path; the local version is committed beside it as `<name>.conflict-<yyyymmdd>.md`
with `conflictOf:`. Nothing is discarded and the queue never jams. On 401/403, pause and send the
user to settings.

## Service worker

Registered `{type: 'module'}` so it can import `shared/apps.js`. A version constant names the
cache; install precaches the shell. Same-origin requests are cache-then-revalidate.

Requests to `api.github.com` **bypass the worker entirely** — caching an API response would hand
back a stale ETag and silently break sync.

A new worker waits; the UI offers "Update ready — reload" and `skipWaiting()` runs only on tap.

## Token and CSP

Stored plaintext in IndexedDB with its expiry: as safe as the unlocked device. The threat that
matters is injected script on our own origin, closed off by policy rather than encryption:

```
default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://api.github.com
```

**No CDNs, ever.** Dependencies are committed to `/shared/vendor/`, pinned by hand, with source
URL and version in `VENDOR.md`. The token is never written to a log, a URL, or the DOM.

The OAuth device flow is not an option: GitHub's `login/device/code` endpoints send no CORS
headers, so a fine-grained PAT is the only no-backend path.

## Dependencies

| What | Why not hand-rolled |
| --- | --- |
| `js-yaml` | Files are hand-edited and must parse as real YAML — quoting, multiline scalars, flow maps. A subset parser misreads them silently. |
| `rrule` | `FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=-1FR` and DST-crossing weeklies are where hand-rolled expansion is wrong without telling you. |

YAML *writing* is ours (~20 lines): we control the output shape, so no dumper is needed.

**Load with `CORE_SCHEMA`, never js-yaml's default.** The default is YAML 1.1 and parses
`start: 2026-04-18` into a JS Date at UTC midnight — silently shifting every all-day entry by a
day east of UTC. `CORE_SCHEMA` keeps it a string and still handles bools, numbers, flow maps and
quoted scalars. This is the same off-by-one the bare-date format exists to prevent, arriving
through the parser instead.

## Platform findings

Verified in both installed home-screen apps (iPhone/Safari, Pixel/Chrome); screenshots in
`spike/res/`.

| | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Storage shared across paths | **Yes.** A marker written by `/mine/spike/` was read back byte-identical by `/mine/spike/sub/`, both reporting `STANDALONE`. Cross-path module imports work too. |
| `{type:'module'}` service worker | Registers on Safari as well as Chrome. No classic fallback needed. |
| `storage.persisted()` | **Already granted**, no prompt, on both. An installed app is exempt from the ~7-day eviction that applies to uninstalled sites, so the token and mirror survive idle periods. |
| Quota | 35 GB (iPhone), 56 GB (Pixel), against a mirror measured in single-digit MB. |

Not tested, and no longer relevant: whether separately-installed PWAs get isolated storage. That
expectation is why the one-app topology was chosen.

Re-run `spike/` after a major iOS release — two of the four results above contradicted the
documented platform behaviour, and that is exactly the kind of thing that regresses silently.

Calendar is an app of [Mine](../REQUIREMENTS.md) to manage your calendar. Every entry is one
markdown file in the data repo, so your calendar stays readable and portable without this app.

See [TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md) for the file format.

## What an entry holds

A title, a type — **event** or **task** — a start and end, a group, a location, participants,
alerts, and a free markdown body for the agenda, checklist or notes.

A task can be ticked done. An event cannot. Entries can repeat, and a repeating entry can have
single occurrences skipped, moved or ticked off without affecting the rest.

## Layout

A navigation pane at the top and a big calendar window below it.

In the top pane, from left to right:

- Left/right buttons to move to the previous/next day, week, month or year, depending on the
  current view.
- The current day/week/month/year, with a small downward arrow for a dropdown date picker. The
  dropdown shows a month at a time, with its name top left and left/right arrows top right.
  Clicking the month name switches to a year grid of 9 years ending with the current one, whose
  arrows page by 9 years.
- A dropdown to choose the view: day, week, month or year.
- A dropdown to filter by group. Each group shows its colour; double-clicking one lets you edit
  its label and colour.

All views show **7 columns, Monday to Sunday**, with weekends tinted so the work week still
reads as a block. A Saturday task has to be visible.

## Views

- **Year** — every month, each with a `M T W T F S S` header row and one row per week. The
  current day is highlighted. A day with entries takes the background colour of its group, split
  between colours if there are several. Clicking a day shows that day's entries. Groups switched
  off in the filter are not shown.
- **Month** — one row per week. Entries appear as rows inside each day cell, sorted by time, all
  day items first. Tasks have a rectangular icon on the right to tick them done. Clicking empty
  space in a cell creates an entry; clicking an entry opens it.
- **Week** — columns are the days, rows are the 24 hours.
- **Day** — the week view for a single day, with more detail per entry.

## Entry popup

A title row; below it a button group to choose the type; below that the remaining fields; below
those an auto-growing monospace box holding the markdown body. A `discard` and a `save` button
at the bottom.

The body is written and shown as raw markdown, so what you see is exactly what lands in the file.

## On a phone

The views above describe the desktop. On a phone a month cell is about 50px wide, so entry rows
are neither readable nor tappable. The same screens adapt:

- The top pane collapses to `[<] [April 2026 v] [=]`.
- Month and year cells show group-coloured dots instead of rows of text.
- Tapping a day opens a sheet listing that day's entries, each one tappable, with an
  `+ add entry` button — so nothing is ever smaller than a finger.

## On the main screen

The tile screen of the main app shows today's entries and the next one coming up.

# Calendar — technical requirements

File format and rendering for [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md). Sync, caching and writes are
in [../TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](../TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md).

## Paths

```
calendar/2026/04/2026-04-18-1400-k3f9.md     one-off entry
calendar/2026/04/2026-04-25-0000-ov1q.md     occurrence override
calendar/recurring/trash-p7qm.md             entry with a recurrence rule
calendar/groups.md                           group -> colour and label
```

The whole folder is mirrored locally, so the path is not a loading optimisation. It is for
humans: the repo browses chronologically on github.com, and no directory grows past a month of
entries. `-k3f9` is 4 random characters, **not** a counter — two devices creating entries offline
on the same day must never mint the same name. No title slug, so retitling is never a rename.

**The path is never the source of truth.** It is derived from `start` at creation; after a move
or an override the two can disagree. Always read `start`. Changing an entry's date is a rename,
which is a delete plus a create in one commit.

Entries with a `recurrence:` rule live in `recurring/` rather than the date tree, because an
open-ended rule must render in months it was not created in and there is no month folder to find
it under.

## Frontmatter

RFC 5545 (iCalendar) naming wherever one exists, so `.ics` export is close to a field copy.
**Empty keys are omitted, never written as `None`** — `None` is a YAML string, not null, and a
parser hands back the text `"None"`.

| Key | Applies to | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | both | required |
| `type` | both | `event` or `task` |
| `start` | both | `DTSTART`. A bare date (`2026-04-18`) is all-day; a timestamp (`2026-04-18T14:00:00Z`) is an instant |
| `end` | both | same value types as `start`; omitted when a single all-day item |
| `group` | both | a name, resolved through `groups.md` |
| `done` | `task` only | `true` / `false` |
| `location` | both | free text |
| `alerts` | both | minutes before start, `0` = at start. Stored and exported only; nothing fires in the background |
| `participants` | both | list of email addresses |
| `recurrence` | both | RRULE string, e.g. `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=SA` |
| `exdate` / `rdate` | recurring | occurrences to skip / extra occurrences |
| `series` | override | id of the recurring file it belongs to |
| `recurrence-id` | override | the original occurrence date this file replaces |
| `conflictOf` | conflict file | written by sync |

No `duration` key — it is `end - start`.

Type and time are independent: `type` decides whether the entry can be ticked done, the value
type of `start` decides whether it is all-day or timed. A task is usually all-day, but may carry
a time and then renders at it.

The bare-date form matters. An all-day task stored as `2026-04-18T00:00:00Z` lands on the wrong
day outside UTC and shifts twice a year on DST.

The markdown body is the entry's content and is preserved byte-for-byte by anything that does not
explicitly edit it.

## Overrides

A recurring file states the rule only. Anything that happens to a *single* occurrence — ticked,
moved, retitled, cancelled — is an override file in the date tree carrying `series:` and
`recurrence-id:`, holding only the keys that differ. The rule file is never rewritten, and since
each override is a fresh path it cannot conflict, even when two devices do it offline.

`exdate:` covers a plain skip where there is nothing to record.

## Rendering a range

1. Collect dated entries whose `start` falls in the range.
2. Expand every rule in `recurring/` over the range; drop dates in `exdate`, add `rdate`.
3. Replace an occurrence with the override matching `series` + `recurrence-id`; an override
   marked cancelled removes it.
4. Drop groups switched off in the filter.
5. Sort: all-day first, then by start time.

Index overrides by `` `${series}|${recurrenceId}` `` once per load; a linear scan per occurrence
is what makes month views slow.

## RRULE

Full RRULE on read — files may be hand-written or imported. The UI only *writes* daily / weekly /
monthly / yearly with `INTERVAL`, `BYDAY`, `UNTIL`, `COUNT`.

`rrule.js` works in UTC. For an all-day rule, set `DTSTART` to UTC midnight and read only the
year/month/day back, never `getDate()` on a local Date — east of UTC that returns the previous
day. `UNTIL` must be written in the `Z` form.

## Groups

`groups.md` is a markdown file whose frontmatter maps a group name to a colour and a label. An
entry stores the name, so recolouring or relabelling is a one-file edit instead of a rewrite of
every entry, and there is no cap on the number of groups. Unknown group renders grey. It lives in
the data repo, so the mapping follows you across devices.

## Widget

`widget.js` exports `summary()`, returning today's entries and the next upcoming one for the main
app's tile screen.

rrule behaves correctly from disk. Before writing code, the judgement calls I'm making — all flagged because the specs don't settle them:

| Question | Decision |
|---|---|
| Which day cell does `start: …T14:00:00Z` land in? | The viewer's **local** day (it's an instant). All-day bare dates are used verbatim, never converted. |
| Filename time digits for a timed entry | **UTC** components, matching `2026-04-18-1400-k3f9.md` ⇄ `start: 2026-04-18T14:00:00Z`. Device-independent, mirrors the stored string. |
| `recurring/` filename stem | Slug of the title + 4 random chars (`take-out-the-trash-p7qm.md`). **Never renamed on retitle** — `series:` references it, so the id must be permanent. |
| What marks an override cancelled | `status: cancelled` (RFC 5545 naming, as the spec's convention says). The UI's own "skip" writes `exdate` on the series instead, per spec. |
| Recurrence-id value | The occurrence's original `start` in the series' value type — bare date for all-day, `…Z` for timed. Matches the sample. |
| Multi-day `end` | Entry renders in its `start` cell only; the spec's range algorithm is start-only. No spanning bars. |
| Recurrence editing UI | A raw `RRULE` text field, not a builder. Full RRULE on read; a daily/weekly/monthly builder is the later job. |
